add.statement:
Fix the admissible extraction parameters and matrix $M$. Let $\mathsf D$ be a target expression, $\chi\in\mathbb F_q$ and $r,r'\in\mathbb F_q^{N+1}$. Use its matrices $W_c^{\mathsf s}$ and vectors $u_c^{\mathsf s}$.
(a) If $\mathsf D$ is $\chi\kappa$ identically at $r$, each sector stack passes and satisfies the ties, $W_c^{\mathsf s}r=u_c^{\mathsf s}$ for all cells, and the plain key-cell corner is $\chi$.
(b) Zero stacks in (a) imply a formal identity.
(c) Without that identity at fixed $r$, the coincidence probability over uniform valid coins is at most $d_f/(q-D)\le\varepsilon_f$.
The difference $G_T-\mathsf K^\alpha$ of the two received target-group expressions has zero stacks in both sectors.
(e) A formally distinct pair in the same source group has coincidence probability at most $\varepsilon_f$ over uniform valid coins at every fixed $r$.
For an identity in (a), each coefficient with right index $H^{\mathrm{leg}}_{j,1}$ in either sector vanishes unless its left index is $F^{k_1}_{i,1}$, in which case it equals the same sector coefficient on $F^{k_1}_{i,2},H^{\mathrm{leg}}_{j,2}$. The kind $\mathrm X$ and exponent in $s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_c}y_i$ identify cell $c$ and row $i$. Formally equal target-group expressions have equal stacks.
Use $d_f=3D+2n+2K_1+6$ and $\varpi=\Omega_{22}\zeta\zeta^{\prime}\zeta^{\prime\prime}\varepsilon$. Factor symbols ending in 1 or 2 are published left or right coordinates, and $W_c,u_c$ omit the current sector index. Use coordinates $x=y-B(\tau)$ and write $\widehat a$ for the exponent of a first-group leaf $a$ at $x=0$, $\Omega_{22}=0$. Write $\beta_{a,j,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}$ for the coefficient with $H_{j,1}$ minus the $F_{i,2},H_{j,2}$ coefficient in the same cell and sector when $a=F_{i,1}$. For $v=\mathrm{quo},\mathrm{rem}$, let $(\Delta_v,Z_{c,v})$ be $(\Delta,Z_c)$ and $(\Delta^{\prime},Z_0)$ respectively. In the selected sector $\mathsf s$ set $H_{c,v}(X)=\sum_{k,j}\mathsf D_{\mathsf P_k^v,(\mathsf B_{c,j}^v)^{\mathsf s}}X^{k+j\Delta_v}$ over the published pairs, and write $(h_c,R_c)=(H_{c,\mathrm{quo}},H_{c,\mathrm{rem}})$. Let $(M_{\mathrm X},N_{\mathrm X})$ be $(\eta_1z_\circ+\eta_2z_+,\eta_2z_-+\eta_3z_\circ)$ for $\mathrm X\in\{\mathrm E,\mathrm O\}$ and $(\eta_3z_+-\eta_1z_-,0)$ for $\mathrm X=\mathrm V$. Also the first mark is charged with probability at most $N_{\mathrm{cmp}}(u)(\theta+\varepsilon_f)+(\binom{L+3u}{2}+L+3u)\varepsilon_f$ for $u=2Q+2$. Every run reaching the target has a first mark which is $\mathsf{init}$, $\mathsf{guess}$, charged or good. Group by nonconstant guess part with a virtual key in class zero.
add.proof:
For fixed $r$, multiplying $\operatorname{val}(\mathsf D)-\chi\kappa$ by $\varpi$ gives a polynomial of degree at most $d_f$ by the degree demand.
The factor $\varpi$ is nonzero on their support because its five factors are sampled nonzero.
For a nonzero cleared polynomial, the incoming demand bounds its probability of vanishing over uniform valid coins by $d_f/(q-D)\le\varepsilon_f$.
By the Schwartz–Zippel demand a polynomial of degree at most $d_f$ that vanishes on all valid coins is zero, so identity on the valid grid is equivalent to the cleared polynomial being zero.
For an identity divide by $\varpi$ in the Laurent ring in its factors, where $y$ and $\tau$ are still polynomial variables.
Taking the $x_j\Omega_{22}^{-1}$ coefficient in positive $\Omega_{12}$ powers of the identity gives $0=\Omega_{12}\sum_{a,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}\beta_{a,j,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}\widehat a\alpha_{\mathsf s}s_{\mathrm{leg}}$ by the hidden-basis formulas.
The values of $\widehat a$ are $1,\zeta\tau^k,\zeta'\tau^k,\zeta''B_i(\tau),\pi_{k_1}B_i(\tau),\Omega_{12}\pi_{k_1}B_i(\tau)$ by their exponent formulas.
The polynomials $B_i$ are independent because their evaluations at the $d_j$ give the identity matrix.
The kind and exponent recover $k_2,k_1$ by quotient and remainder of half the exponent rounded down modulo $K_1$, with $k_1=0$ for a leg.
At $\varepsilon^0$ the product $\pi_{k_1}s_{\mathrm{leg}}$ is $\pi s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_c}$ by the scalar formulas.
Taking that coefficient in this extracted identity leaves distinct monomials in the sector, scalars, and $\upsilon$, except for the indexed families $B_i$ or distinct powers of $\tau$.
Hence independence of these families in their respective monomials gives $\beta_{a,j,\mathrm{leg},\mathsf s}=0$ for all indices.
In the original $y$ coordinates take the component of $\pi$-degree one, zero degrees in $\zeta,\zeta',\zeta''$, and total hidden-basis degree zero, separately for each power of $\alpha$.
The paired coefficient in the selected sector equals $\chi_{\mathsf s}\kappa$ after moving the key leaf to the right, with $\chi_{\mathrm{plain}}=\chi$ and $\chi_\alpha=-\mathsf D_K$.
From the leaf formulas these pairs are matched $F,H$ terms, $F_{i,1}$ with search bases or $G_2$, quotient and remainder powers with corresponding bases, and $Y_i$ with cancellation bases.
Matched pairs give $F_i^{k_1}H_j^{\mathrm{leg}}$ because $\Omega\Omega^{-1}=1$.
Multiplication of these two coordinates gives $F_i^{k_1}H_j^{\mathrm{leg}}=\gamma_c(y_i r_j+y_iA_j-A_i y_j+A_iB_j)+\pi_{k_1}y_i\vartheta_{\mathrm{leg},j}$, with $A_i,B_i$ evaluated at $\tau$.
The pairing contribution of kind $v$ to cell $c$ is $\gamma_c Z_{c,v}(\tau)H_{c,v}(\tau)$ by cancellation of the reciprocal scalar in its two leaf formulas.
The ranges of $k,j$ and $\nu\mid\Delta'$ give only allowed exponents $k+j\Delta'<J'\Delta'=\nu n_{\mathsf c}$ in $R_c$.
Collecting the terms containing $s_{\mathrm X}$ gives $\sum_c\gamma_c b_c$ with $b_c=y^\top(W_c r-u_c)+y^\top(W_c-W_c^\top)A(\tau)+(P_{W_c}+h_c Z_c+Z_0R_c)(\tau)$.
The other terms contain no $s_{\mathrm X}$ because tie masks, cancellation bases and the generator lack these factors.
The coefficient of $\pi s_{\mathrm X}\upsilon^{k_c}\varepsilon^0$ gives $b_c=\chi_{\mathsf s}L_\rho$ at the key cell and zero at every other cell.
The matrix with columns $(1,A(\tau))$ at $d_0,\rho,d_1,\ldots,d_N$ is invertible by subtracting the $d_0$ column and using the QAP table.
Multiplying the evaluated $y$-coefficient equations by its inverse gives $[W_c r-u_c\mid W_c-W_c^\top]=0$.
Evaluating the constant-in-$y$ key identity at $\tau=\rho$ gives $(W_{c_{\mathrm{key}}})_{00}=\chi_{\mathsf s}$ by the QAP table and the vanishing of $Z_c,Z_0$ there.
The QAP criterion makes every $W_c$ pass by its constant-in-$y$ identity with quotient $-h_c$ and allowed remainder $-R_c$.
The $\varepsilon^0$ coefficient of $\pi_{k_1}\vartheta_{\mathrm{leg}}$ is $\pi[\upsilon^{k_c}M_{\mathrm X}-(-\omega\upsilon)^{k_c}N_{\mathrm X}]$ by multiplying the mask factors.
Summing these contributions against $y^\top W_c$ gives $\pi\sum_a\eta_a y^\top t_a(\upsilon)$ by the defining three tie polynomials.
The other terms of $\eta_a\varepsilon^0$ are from the tie bases and have factor $P(\upsilon)$.
Extracting the $\pi\eta_a\varepsilon^0 y_i$ coefficient with zero $s_{\mathrm X}$ degrees from the class identity gives $(t_a)_i=0\pmod P$ for every $a,i$.
For zero stacks changing $r$ to any $r^{\prime}$ changes no value because every supported coefficient of an $r$-dependent leaf is a stack entry.
For a formal identity the equations $W_c r'=u_c$ for arbitrary $r'$ force $W_c=0$.
Applying this result to the difference of formally equal expressions shows their stacks agree.
The received target difference and any source-group difference paired with the opposite generator have zero stacks because the stack projection kills generator-containing pairs and the key term.
A formally distinct source pair makes its generator-paired difference nonformal by nondegeneracy.
By the zero-stack result, this nonformal difference is nonidentical at every fixed $r$.
The target coincidence bound at each such $r$ bounds the original comparison by $\varepsilon_f$.
Truncating at the caps preserves real runs by hypothesis.
The target query sets a mark by (M4) if there is none.
The mark rules give exactly the four stated kinds.
The stopped transcript and setup coins fix the first mark, so its law is the same in $\mathsf R_\$$.
By (P2) each group has more than $L+3Q$ labels for symbolic entries.
The lazy coupling shares requests up to the first evaluation collision.
Under it noncolliding entries evaluate to the real exponents.
The symbolic transcript is independent of evaluation because it uses label images, formal rules and independent oracle and mask coins.
A charged first mark excludes a collision on received labels by (M1).
A good collision cannot introduce a fresh guess, which would occur in the difference.
A good result collision merges with the earlier label by equality of exponents.
Such a merge before the target query would set a good mark by (M3).
On a charged run a target query before collision must find an entry by (M4).
The coupling makes that entry a key value.
It must be bad by (M4) because the first mark is charged.
Thus (M3)–(M4) force a bad symbolic collision or key value on a charged run.
The linear and pairing rules give a guess polynomial with source or constant coefficients in degree one and constant coefficients in degree two.
For each fixed $r$, some formally nonzero guess coefficient is nonzero on the valid grid by source nonidentity.
Thus the cleared polynomial is nonzero since $\varpi$ never vanishes there.
The cleared total degree is at most $\max(d_f,d_f+1,5+2)=d_f+1$ by the target and source degree bounds and the five factors of $\varpi$.
The coin domains each have at least $q-D$ choices by the exclusions and $K_1+1\le D$.
Schwartz–Zippel bounds the event by $(d_f+1)/(q-D)\le\varepsilon_f$.
For a guess-free nonidentity use the bound $\varepsilon_f$ from (c) and (e).
At a guess-free identity the mark stack is nonzero by the zero-stack and key-corner conclusions.
A bad identity therefore has a light mark stack by definition.
The identity locus is in a fiber of that stack by (a).
The union bound on the light-stack fiber and the nonidentity coincidence gives $\theta+\varepsilon_f$ per guess-free bad event.
The exposure budget gives at most $\binom{L+3Q}{2}+L+3Q$ pairs and single entries with guesses.
Outside results, a class has at most one raw guess or the received entries and virtual key, by distinct guess variables.
Counting same-class pairs by result order and including received key pairs gives at most $L+\sum_{j=1}^Q(L+j)\le N_{\mathrm{cmp}}(u)$ guess-free events.
Union bounding at fixed symbolic transcript gives the stated estimate using $Q\le u$.
Average over the transcript since the estimate is independent of it.

add.statement: Every nonzero usable stack of rank at most three whose row space contains no kernel vector has a witness of $S$ in its row space. For the proof, $V$ is the base-field row space of the stack and $d=\dim V$. Write $K=\mathbb F_{q^n}$, $V_K=K\otimes_{\mathbb F_q} V$, $V_K^*=\operatorname{Hom}_K(V_K,K)$, and use $a=n/2-1$, $b=n/2$, $c=n/2+1$. Put $(Z_a,Z_b,Z_c)=(W_U,W_V,\sigma^c(W_U))$, $h_s=\sigma^s(z)|_V$ extended to $V_K$, and $\ell_i$ the restriction of coordinate $i$ to $V$. On forms and tensors Frobenius acts on coefficients in a base-field basis. A tensor $w^{\otimes j}$ on the dual denotes the product of the $j$ evaluations at $w$. Use $U$ for the annihilator of $V_K$ in the ambient dual. Set-indexed tensor coordinates depend only on the set of positive basis indices. Let $\mathcal B$ be the space of symmetric bilinear forms on $V_K^*$ whose pullbacks to the ambient dual are annihilated by all tests. Let $\varrho$ range over the base-field test functionals. A $\varrho$-contraction of $L$ applies $\varrho$ to its last two factors. For the Boolean points below use $T_{s,\delta}=z_\delta\sigma^s(z_\delta)w_\delta^{\otimes2}$. Denote the Boolean test on $(\ell_i,\ell_i-\ell_0)$ by $\varrho_i$.
add.proof:
The radical of the symmetric form given by each $W_c$ contains $U$, since its rows lie in $V_K$.
Each $W_c$ descends under restriction to a form in $\mathcal B$, whose pullback is the original passing form.
The $Z_s$ lie in $\mathcal B$ by their defining linear combinations.
Reducing the three tie polynomials modulo $P$ via $\sigma^j(z)=z[\omega^jT]$ gives $Z_s(h_t,-)=Z_t(h_s,-)$ for the three pairs from $a,b,c$.
The Moore determinant demand makes $h_a,\ldots,h_{a+d-1}$ a basis of $V_K^*$ in coordinates of a basis of $V$, whose images under $\sigma^a z$ are independent by injectivity.
For any relation $\sum_s\lambda_s h_s=0$ among the three inputs, the ties give $(\sum_s\lambda_s Z_s)(h_t,-)=Z_t(\sum_s\lambda_s h_s,-)=0$ for each $t$.
The $h_t$ span the dual, so $\sum_s\lambda_s Z_s=0$.
Thus the assignment extends to a linear map into $\mathcal B$, defining $L$ by $L(h_s,-,-)=Z_s$ for all three inputs.
The tie equations on pairs of spanning inputs make $L$ symmetric in its first two slots.
The first-two and last-two transpositions generate all permutations, so $L$ is fully symmetric.
At least one of $L(h_a,-,-),L(h_b,-,-)$ is nonzero by coefficient extraction from the nonzero stack.
Every $\varrho$-contraction of $L$ is zero by its first-slot map into $\mathcal B$.
The Frobenius definition gives $Z_a=\sigma^a(Z_c)$ since $a+c=n$.
The even exponents of $W_V$ give $Z_b=\sigma^b(Z_b)$ since $\sigma^b(T)=-T$.
If $\ell_0=0$, choose a dual basis from the remaining coordinate forms.
The zero $\varrho_i$ contractions then make all repeated-index coordinates vanish by symmetry.
Since $L\ne0$, a triple of distinct basis inputs must exist, using all three basis inputs when $d\le3$.
As $L$ is supported on permutations of that triple with value $t$ there, its contraction $Z_s$ at $h_s$ has complementary off-diagonal entries $t(h_s)_k$ by trilinearity, where $(h_s)_k$ are coordinates in this basis.
Comparing these entries in the two Frobenius identities gives $t h_s=\sigma^s(t)h_0$ for $s=a,b$, since $\sigma^a(h_c)=\sigma^b(h_b)=h_0$.
The two independent inputs $h_a,h_b$ cannot both be multiples of $h_0$, contradicting $t\ne0$.
Thus $\ell_0\ne0$.
The restricted coordinate forms span the dual, so extend $\ell_0$ to a dual basis with $\ell_{i_1},\ldots,\ell_{i_{d-1}}$.
For each $\delta\in\{0,1\}^{d-1}$ take the unique $w_\delta\in V$ with basis values $(1,\delta)$.
The zero $\varrho_{i_j}$ contraction gives $L(-,\ell_{i_j},\ell_{i_j})=L(-,\ell_{i_j},\ell_0)$.
By symmetry and these reductions each basis-triple coordinate depends only on its set of positive basis indices.
An evaluation tensor $w_\delta^{\otimes j}$ has coordinate value one exactly when the set of positive basis indices in that coordinate is contained in the support of $\delta$, and zero otherwise.
Möbius inversion makes $w_\delta^{\otimes j}$ a basis of the set-indexed $j$-tensors for $j=2,3$ since every subset occurs among $j$ slots.
Set $z_\delta=h_0(w_\delta)$, which is nonzero by injectivity of $z$ on $V$ and $\ell_0(w_\delta)=1$.
With $x_\delta$ the coordinates of $L$ in the cubic basis $z_\delta w_\delta^{\otimes3}$, contraction gives $Z_s=\sum_\delta x_\delta T_{s,\delta}$.
The $T_{s,\delta}$ coordinate of the Frobenius identity gives $x_\delta-\sigma^s(x_\delta)=0$ for $s=a,b$ by cyclicity $\sigma^n=1$.
The common fixed field of $\sigma^a$ and $\sigma^b$ is $\mathbb F_q$ by the finite-field subfield theorem since $\gcd(a,b)=1$.
Apply $(z|_V)^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_V$ to the zero $\varrho$-contraction in $z(V)\otimes_{\mathbb F_q}V$ using the cubic coordinates $x_\delta$, giving $\sum_\delta x_\delta\varrho(w_\delta^{\otimes2})w_\delta^{\otimes2}=0$.
Independence of the pair tensors gives $x_\delta\varrho(w_\delta^{\otimes2})=0$ for every $\delta$.
For a nonzero coordinate $x_\delta$ of $L$, the coefficient equations give vanishing of every test on $w_\delta^{\otimes2}$ by division by $x_\delta$.
Since $(w_\delta)_0=1$, the Booleanity equivalence for its moment matrix gives $(w_\delta)_i\in\{0,1\}$ for all $i>0$.
The constraint equivalence for the same moment matrix makes every constraint hold.
Thus this Boolean assignment is a witness in $V$ by definition.

add.statement: Under the extraction theorem's hypotheses, if the adversary runs in time $t$ with at most $Q$ generic group calls and $Q_H$ queries to each random oracle, both $\mathcal B_0,\mathcal B_1$ run within $t_R=t+O(Q+d_R Q_H+\mu)+\mathsf{poly}(D,\log q)$ in the specified operations model including description and advice. With valid non-search coordinates fixed, only $H^{\mathrm{leg}}_{j,1}$ and its alpha copy among the received exponents depend on $r$. A record circuit uses the monitor's zero record for an operand without a record. The first mark is $\mathsf{guess}$ with probability at most $2^\lambda/N_{\mathsf{free}}$. In $\mathsf R_\$$ with independent uniform mask $h$, programming the target answer to $h\oplus m$ gives the real law for $m$ and preserves the shared prefix through the first target query before answering, or through output if none. Each generic call exposes at most two operands and one result.
add.proof:
The identities $(k+1)d_R=n$ and $\ell=\lceil N/d_R\rceil$ give $(k+1)(\ell+1)d_R\le D(D+2)$ using $N,n\le D$.
The leaf count $L$ is at most $C(2D+1)^3$ for constant $C$ by the published index ranges and $K_1K_2=n/2$, $1\le J\Delta\le2D$, $1\le J'\max(1,\Delta')\le D$.
The private, recovery and encryption coordinates are sampled in polynomial time by the independent finite-set draws in (R2) and encryption, apart from its centered search coordinate.
The excluded sets for the coin draws have polynomial-size descriptions by their explicit point and left-leg lists.
The centered sampler costs $O(N+1)$ draws and integer operations on values bounded by $B<q\le2^{\ell_{\mathsf{lab}}}$ by its explicit formula.
Evaluating the form definition on coordinate vectors by ordinary ring convolution constructs the $n(N+1)$ coefficients in polynomial time by the ring-size bound.
Hardwire the fixed QAP coefficients into Horner circuits with the scalar-factor gates to obtain polynomial-size advised leaf circuits by the degree bounds.
The masked message takes $O(\mu)$ additional description and operations by packing it into label-sized blocks for writes and XORs.
Represent each uniform injection by the restriction of a uniform bijection to its exponent tokens, with an additional token for each excess label string.
Maintain the exposed part in both directions in tables, recording dummy assignments only as outside-image flags.
By deferred decisions for the bijection, expose the image of an unused exponent by the allowed uniform sample of undecided strings.
For an undecided string expose the uniform remaining preimage by using the allowed uniform unused-exponent sample when a uniform draw in $[0,U-1]$ is below $A$, and marking it outside the image otherwise, where $A$ counts unused exponents and $U<2^{\ell_{\mathsf{lab}}}$ counts undecided strings after generator allocation.
Each generic call uses at most two operand exposures and one result lookup or assignment in the tables, taking the negated exponent for a name request passing its eligibility flag.
Sample each fresh reply componentwise with at most $d_R$ draws, using the field components of a ring reply or the single finite-set component in $\{0,1\}^\mu$ of a key reply.
Each oracle query uses one lookup and at most one insertion, with immutable references as reply values so the caller reads the bits in its own time.
Each group call adds $O(1)$ record gates by the linear, pairing and sign-change rules.
Zeroing the other sector's right-group and key leaves projects precisely to the desired sector by the target expression formula, with generators assigned to the plain sector.
Substituting any fixed valid non-search coordinates in the received leaf formulas leaves only $H^{\mathrm{leg}}_{j,1}$ and its alpha copy dependent on $r$, each affine in $r_j$.
Evaluate each record gate as it is created at the independently presampled private point and six sector-projected recovery points, with constant work per gate at each point.
Use two keep-first slots for (R3), one for the first target-label record and one for the old and new roots of the first $\mathbb G_T$ result with a pre-insertion record of unequal private value.
Reverse differentiation with stored values gives the $r_j$ gradient by summing local derivative-weight products along input edges, seeded by $(1,-1)$ at the difference pointers or $1$ at the target record.
Gaussian elimination finds a nonzero vector when one exists in the span of the three gradients intersected with the $n$ form kernels, in polynomial time by these dimensions and $N\le D$.
Sum these costs with $k\ell d_R$ seeded coefficients, $L+O(1)$ initial labels, $Q_H$ queries per oracle, twelve reverse passes, two polynomial-time lifts by the lifting demand and $\ell d_R$ packing writes to obtain $t_R$.
Programming the target answer in $\mathsf R_\$$ to $h\oplus m$ restores the real law by uniformity conditional on encryption coins and maps.
Programming only the target answer preserves this transcript for each message.
In $\mathsf R_\$$ defer label exposures to received labels and group calls, since the independent mask needs no private target-label assignment.
Before a mark in $\mathsf R_\$$, valid target-group labels exposed this way have entries by (M1)–(M3).
On the common prefix, (M4) makes a first $\mathsf{guess}$ require a query hitting an unexposed target.
Given non-label tapes and exposures in the capped run ignoring marks, deferred sampling gives an unexposed target mass $1/U$ per undecided string, where $U\ge2^{\ell_{\mathsf{lab}}}-L-3Q\ge N_{\mathsf{free}}$.
Union bounding hits of the still-unexposed target over the first $2^\lambda$ key queries within the call cap gives the guess bound.

add.statement:
Let $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb Z^I$ have rank $d\in[3]$, $|I|\le N$ and basis $B$. For nonempty $\Theta$-trimmed box set $F$ on $I\sqcup\{i'\}$ put $\Phi(r)=(B^\top r_I,r_{i'})$.

(a) If $\dim \Phi(F) = d + 1$ and $\Phi(F)$ is in a coset of a subgroup of index $q$ of $\mathbb{Z}^{d+1}$, then $\Pr[F] \le \Lambda_d\, g^d\, h(\Theta)\, m(\Theta)/q$.
(b) If $F^\perp$ has a rank $d'$ with $1 \le d' < d$ and a largest minor at a set $J \subseteq I$, and the restriction to $I$ of each vector of $F^\perp$ lies in $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}(\Theta)$, then $\Pr[F]\, h(F^\perp) \le \Lambda_{d-d'}\, g^{d-d'}\, h(\Theta)\, m(\Theta)$. In (b) let $Y$ be an integer basis matrix of $F^\perp$ and $B_J$ the row restriction. Write $BU=(B_1,B_2)$, $U^\top B^\top r_I=(y_1,y_2)$ and $\Psi(r)=(y_1,y_2,r_{i'})$. Put $k=d+1-d^{\prime}$. In (a) take $d^{\prime}=0$, $J=\varnothing$, $B_2=B$, $U=I_d$, $a=1$, $\delta=q$, $p=\mathrm{id}$. In (b) use a basis matrix $V$ of the integer normal lattice of $\Psi(F)$ with row blocks $V_1,V_2,V_3$ of sizes $d^{\prime},k-1,1$, and set $a=|\det(B_1)_J|$ and $\delta=|\det V_1|$, $\pi(y_2,x)=V_2^\top y_2+V_3^\top x$ modulo $V_1^\top\mathbb Z^{d^{\prime}}$. Put $m=k-1$, let $\mathbb B^I$ and $v_m$ denote the unit ball in $\mathbb R^I$ and unit $m$-ball volume, and write $\mathcal W=\bigwedge_{j=1}^m(B_2)_j$ for the column wedge. Let $U_2$ be the last $m$ columns of $U$. Write $b_F=q$ in (a) and $b_F=h(F^\perp)$ in (b).
add.proof:
For a fixed image pair $(y,x)$ with $x=r_{i'}$ its box density is at most $m(\Theta)/g$, by fixing the new coordinate and counting a fiber of the other coordinates.
Thus $\Pr[F]\le m(\Theta)|\Phi(F)|/g$.
In (b), Smith normal form of the $d^{\prime}\times d$ matrix $B_J$ supplies a unimodular right multiplier $U$ with $(B_2)_J=0$.
The map $(u,t)\mapsto(BUu,t)$ identifies the real normal spaces of $\Psi(F)$ and $F$ by the restriction assumption.
The pullback of the columns of $V$ is $YC$ with $C$ a nonsingular integer matrix, because they are independent integer normals of $F$.
Cauchy–Binet for the $J$-minor of the pullback gives $a\delta=b_F|\det C|$ since $(B_2)_J=0$.
Solving with $V_1^\top$ makes $p(y,x)=((U^\top y)_2,x)$ an affine isomorphism $\operatorname{aff}\Phi(F)\to\mathbb R^k$.
Modulo $V_1^\top\mathbb Z^{d^{\prime}}$, the transpose-surjectivity demand makes $\pi$ onto the order-$\delta$ quotient.
The affine normal equations put all projected points in one $\pi$-fiber, an index-$\delta$ lattice coset.
Triangulate the hull of $p(\Phi(F))$ with every point as a vertex, using stellar subdivision to insert points.
For each full simplex $T$, the lattice determinant formula gives $(k+1)\delta\le (k+1)!\operatorname{vol}(T)$.
Summing over full simplices counts every point at least once, hence $|\Phi(F)|\le (k+1)!V_*/\delta$ for hull volume $V_*$.
The ellipsoid image rule under $U_2^\top$ puts the projected search coordinates in a translate of $(R_{\mathrm{tr}}g/\sqrt{12})B_2^\top\mathbb B^I$ from the original covariance.
The product with the last-coordinate interval has volume at most $g v_m(R_{\mathrm{tr}}g/\sqrt{12})^m\|\mathcal W\|$ by the ball image volume formula and the interval length at most $g$.
Block expansion of $B_{J\cup R}=(BU)_{J\cup R}U^{-1}$ gives $|\det B_{J\cup R}|=a|\det(B_2)_R|$ for disjoint $J,R$ with $|R|=m$.
Thus $a\|\mathcal W\|\le h(\Theta)N^{m/2}$ by the at most $N^m$ potentially nonzero wedge coordinates, all with rows disjoint from $J$.
The estimates bound $b_F\Pr[F]$ by $g^m h(\Theta)m(\Theta)$ times $(m+2)!v_m(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\sqrt N/\sqrt{12})^m$, using $b_F\le a\delta$.
For $(v_1,v_2,v_3)=(2,\pi,4\pi/3)$, condition (I3) bounds this factor by $\Lambda_m$.

add.statement: For a stack $\mathbf W$, $\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)\le g^{-\operatorname{rank}\mathbf W}$ and $\operatorname{gp}(v^\top)\ge\operatorname{gp}(\mathbf W)$ for every row-space vector $v$. Let $A$ stack the rows vertically and let $J$ be its pivots in index order, so a nonzero column zero is a pivot. Raw draws are independent box coordinates, using $r_\star$ in centered slot zero.
add.proof:
With the raw draws off $J$ fixed, column independence allows at most one tuple of sampled pivot coordinates of $r$ per fiber, since a nonpivot column zero has no contribution.
A retained centered coordinate zero determines its raw draw by undoing the known shift modulo $q$, with a unique representative in the length-$g<q$ interval.
Independence bounds the probability of this partial graph by the largest raw pivot atom $g^{-|J|}$.
The linear image $v^\top r$ of the stack output has maximum atom at least that of the stack.

add.statement: For Boolean $w$ with $w_0=1$, both samplers satisfy $|r(w)-c_w|\le B$ and $\|r(w)-c_w\|_2\le g\sqrt{H/12}+\delta$, with $(H,\delta)=(1+\operatorname{wt}(w),1/2)$ and $(1+N/4,3/2)$ respectively. Use the RMS norm and write $M$ for the center before flooring. Let $X$ sum the raw draws centered at $(g+3)/2$ with weights $w$ for independent sampling and $(1,w_1-1/2,\ldots,w_N-1/2)$ for centered sampling, with zeroth draw $r_\star$.
add.proof:
